reason: M8 is a diode-connected PMOS that mainly biases the VOUT1-side PMOS load (M3); if you already provide an external bias or accept a less-controlled operating point, the stage can still pass differential signals. Caveat: removing it can leave M3’s gate/node net030 without a defined DC bias, risking saturation/turn-off and large gain/offset changes.
impact_estimate: Low if an external bias replaces it; moderate-to-high otherwise

reason: M9 is the symmetric diode-connected PMOS bias for the VOUT2-side PMOS load (M7); it’s often redundant if net032 is biased elsewhere or if you tolerate degraded bias stability. Caveat: without M9, net032 may float, which can destabilize M7’s operating point and degrade gain/linearity.
impact_estimate: Low if net032 has another DC bias path; moderate-to-high otherwise

reason: M6 looks like a VB1-controlled NMOS pull-down/clamp at VOUT2; removing it typically preserves the core differential-to-current conversion (M5/M4) and PMOS loads (M3/M7) while reducing output loading. Caveat: output common-mode/swing control at VOUT2 may worsen and the two outputs can become less symmetric if M1 remains.
